YELLOW ROOM · photolithography
light that will not spoil the resist
read it and learn the classes
loading wafers into the hood in full gown
Clean room manager
reviewing the night's particle counts
Inside: move slowly, never run; keep your hands above your waist; nothing from outside comes in that has not been wiped; no paper, no pencils, no phones unless bagged.
Through the air shower to the clean bay.
The air shower needs a level 3 card.
Why: the bench is the line between the dirty side and the clean side; nothing that touched the floor on one side crosses it.
Why: the jets blow loose particles off you; the room you enter allows at most 3,520 particles of 0.5 µm or more in a cubic metre of air.
Why: people are the biggest source of dirt in a clean room: skin, hair, breath and lint.
How many particles of 0.5 µm or larger a cubic metre of air may hold
Each class is ten times cleaner than the one after it.
Air comes down through filters in the ceiling (HEPA: they catch 99.97% of particles at 0.3 µm) and out through the floor, sweeping dirt away from the work.
The room is kept at a slightly higher pressure than the corridor, so air leaks out, never in.
